title: The Stranger Who Caught the Sign
amb: morning sea breeze with distant waves and gulls, a wooden sign creaking on an iron bracket

lines.text: Early morning. The tide is out, the gulls are loud, and you're watering the lavender by the gate.
Above you, the old wooden sign creaks on its iron bracket. Then the creaking stops, and it falls.
You hear a thud, but it isn't wood on stone. It's wood landing in hands. Someone on the other side of your gate has caught it.
Got it. Got it. Nobody panic. Especially the sign.
He's tall, with salt wind in his hair, and he's hugging the sign to his chest. The sage-green gate is waist-high and shut between you. He's an arm's length away.
Then he looks up at you, and his whole face lights up. It's like you're the best part of his morning.
Morning! You're already out here. That's good. That's really good.
You raise the watering can. "Put it down."
This? Your toes might have a problem with that.
You tell him you mean the sign. Put it down, and take a step back.
Okay. Okay. Just so we are clear, I am not waterproof.
He leans the sign against the stone wall, letters facing the stones, and steps back onto the cobbles. His hands are up. He's still smiling.
I'm Rowan. Here to fix the sign.
You've never seen him before. You'd remember a grin like that. You tell him he doesn't look like anyone you hired.
[chuckles softly] Bad introduction. Want me to start over?
You don't answer. Water drips from the spout onto your boot.
Starting over. Hi. Rowan. I fix things. Windows, doors, signs that throw themselves off buildings.
That bracket's been loose for a while. The left hook goes first. It's always the left.
You glance up. The left hook hangs open, bent and rusted. You didn't know that until just now.
So how does a stranger know it?
Gate looks great, by the way. Told you that green would work.
Told you. The words land wrong. The breeze turns cool on your neck, and your grip tightens on the handle.
You take one step back from the gate. You don't say anything. You don't have to.
His smile fades. Quietly, he takes two more steps back across the cobbles, until the whole path lies between you.
[quietly] Too much. Sorry. I'll stay right here.
He waits. He doesn't argue, and he doesn't reach for the latch. He just watches you like your answer matters.
You don't have to take my word for anything. I've got a tool bag. Very official. Very boring.
Or there's Nora. She'll vouch for me. Probably while rolling her eyes.
Next door, an oven door bangs. Warm bread smell drifts over the wall. Through the bakery window, a shadow moves behind the glass.
A gull cries overhead. The sign rests against your wall. Your name is hidden against the stone.
The gate is still shut. And he's still looking at you as if he knows you.

prompt: A stranger who knows your gate a little too well is waiting on the other side. How will you check who he is?
choices: I aim the can at him: open your tool bag, slowly.
I shout toward the bakery window for Nora to vouch.
